newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian roasters expect sharp hike in prices.
newsitem.headline: Belgian roasters expect sharp hike in prices.

text.p: Belgian roasted coffee prices will rise sharply in April a spokesman for the country's coffee roasters association said on Thursday.
The association expects consumer prices to rise between 20 to 40 Belgian francs a kilo, depending on quality, the spokesman added.

Saying that increases will be due to higher green coffee prices the spokesman said in a statement: "The association expects roasted coffee prices to increase between 20 and 40 Belgian francs a kilogram in April."

The country now operates a free market in coffee and roasters no longer have to agree price rises with the government, leaving traders to set their own, which are expected to take place throughout the month.
Roasters have published statistics of green coffee exports and imports for the first time in their national coffee report for 1996.
The report based on Belgian Coffee Federation statistics show that green coffee imports at 1,937,701 bags exceeded exports at 261,821 bags.
Green coffee stocks at the port of Antwerp stood at 564,217 bags on February 28 compared with 370,500 bags on October 31, 1996.
For the first time, statistics provided by the Belgian Coffee Federation on imports and exports of roasted coffee put Germany as the top exporter to Belgium, the report said.
